title: Model Contents (Textable, Record)
description: Complete repository structure with all files and directories for a model
documentation:
## Purpose
Provides a detailed inventory of all files and directories in a model repository, including sizes, checksums, and local availability. This allows callers to inspect exactly what a model package contains before or after downloading.

## When to use
Use this type when a user or orchestrator needs to understand which files make up a model, verify checksums, or determine which files have already been downloaded. It is the output of a model-contents inspection cap.

## Notes
The `all_files` array is a flat listing of every entry in the repository. The optional `root` object provides the same information as a hierarchy for UIs that need a tree view. The `metadata` object contains repository-level information such as tags or licence identifiers if the repository exposes them.

## Textable
Coercion marker indicating the value is faithfully representable as UTF-8 text.
Strings are textable trivially; integers and booleans are textable via their
string form; structured values are textable when JSON-serialised. Binary blobs
(images, audio, raw bytes) are NOT textable — converting them to text requires
explicit transformation that may be lossy.

The value is faithfully representable as UTF-8 text without loss.

## Record marker
Presence marker indicating the value's content is a key-value mapping at its
root: a JSON object, a CSV row with named columns, a TOML table, an INI file.
Independent of `list-marker` — a value can be both (a list of records),
either alone, or neither.

The value's content is a key-value mapping. Consumers can expect to address
fields by name.
